# awscc_glue_session (Resource)

Resource Type definition for AWS::Glue::Session. Sessions provide an on-demand, serverless Apache Spark runtime environment for building, testing, and running data preparation and analytics applications.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `command` (Attributes) The SessionCommand that runs the job. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command))
- `role` (String) The IAM Role ARN.
- `session_id` (String) The ID of the session.

### Optional

- `connections` (Attributes) Specifies the connections used by the session. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connections))
- `default_arguments` (Map of String) A map array of key-value pairs. Max is 75 pairs.
- `description` (String) The description of the session.
- `glue_version` (String) The Glue version determines the versions of Apache Spark and Python that Glue supports. The GlueVersion must be greater than 2.0.
- `idle_timeout` (Number) The number of minutes when idle before session times out. Default is the value of Timeout.
- `max_capacity` (Number) The number of Glue data processing units (DPUs) that can be allocated when the job runs.
- `number_of_workers` (Number) The number of workers of a defined WorkerType to use for the session.
- `request_origin` (String) The origin of the request.
- `security_configuration` (String) The name of the SecurityConfiguration structure to be used with the session.
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags belonging to the session. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `timeout` (Number) The number of minutes before session times out.
- `worker_type` (String) The type of predefined worker that is allocated when a session runs.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the session.
- `created_on` (String) The time and date when the session was created.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `progress` (Number) The code execution progress of the session.
- `status` (String) The session status.

<a id="nestedatt--command"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command`

Optional:

- `name` (String) Specifies the name of the SessionCommand. Can be 'glueetl' or 'gluestreaming'.
- `python_version` (String) Specifies the Python version. The Python version indicates the version supported for jobs of type Spark.


<a id="nestedatt--connections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `connections`

Optional:

- `connections` (List of String) A list of connection names used by the session.


<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Optional:

- `key` (String) The key name of the tag.
- `value` (String) The value for the tag.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_glue_session.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the session

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_glue_session.example
  id = "arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_glue_session.example "arn"
```
